title: Riyadh Factory Fire Kills 16 Bangladeshi Workers
detail: A fire broke out at an unlicensed furniture-upholstery facility in Riyadh's Musa Sanaiya industrial area, killing 16 Bangladeshi migrant workers. Saudi Civil Defence extinguished the blaze; no cause was formally disclosed. Bangladesh's embassy in Riyadh worked with Saudi authorities to identify victims and coordinate repatriation of remains, with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman directing ministries to speed the process and secure compensation. Saudi Arabia hosts an estimated 3.5 million Bangladeshi workers, who remitted over $2.7 billion home in the past year, putting renewed scrutiny on labor and workplace-safety conditions in the Kingdom's informal manufacturing sector.

title: Houthi Drone Strike Hits Aramco's Jazan Refinery
detail: A Houthi drone struck Saudi Aramco's 400,000 bpd Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast, sparking a fire that Aramco firefighting teams brought under control by dawn; the Saudi Energy Ministry reported no injuries. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree called it a 'precise' strike carried out in response to alleged Saudi violations of Yemeni airspace. It was the second reported Houthi strike on the Jazan complex in under two weeks, after a July 27 attack allegedly damaged the facility's gasification unit and tank farm, underscoring the growing risk to Saudi oil infrastructure from the Houthis' declared Red Sea blockade.
